4 MapSketch include sketch showing the t: The total area of operations spans a 3.0-mile radius around the Blackwood Industrial Corridor. The primary incident site is Pipeline Valve Station 14-B along Blackwood River Road. Impacted areas include a 150-foot radius around the breached 8-inch pressurized line releasing anhydrous ammonia gas and 1,000 yards of shoreline along the Blackwood River. Threatened areas include Oakridge Residential Subdivision 0.75 miles downwind to the East and the Valley Water Authority Municipal Intake Facility 1.5 miles downstream. State police aviation observed a dense, low-hanging vapor cloud moving downwind and a localized surface sheen on the riverbank. The toxic vapor plume is moving East-Northeast at 6 mph, and waterborne chemical runoff is traveling downstream at approximately 2.0 knots.
5 Situation Summary and Health and Safet: At 06:50, a third-party excavation crew punctured the main transfer pipeline, causing an uncontrolled high-pressure hazardous-material release. Hazards include severe anhydrous ammonia vapor exposure, cryogenic freeze burns, respiratory injury, structural eye damage, heat stress in 85°F temperatures, and slip-and-fall risks near steep river embankments. Establish a 500-foot Exclusion Zone. Hot Zone entry requires Level A vapor-tight PPE with SCBA. Maintain continuous photoionization detector monitoring at control perimeters, deploy water curtains for vapor knockdown, and require full-body chemical decontamination at the Warm-to-Cold Zone boundary.
7 Current and Planned Objectives: Isolate the pipeline segment by closing upstream valves by 09:30; complete shelter-in-place and partial evacuation of 120 homes in the downwind Oakridge subdivision by 10:00; deploy absorbent and containment boom across the Blackwood River above the municipal water intake by 10:30; and establish a Multi-Agency Unified Command at the Regional Emergency Operations Center by 11:00.
